def transform(grid):
    # Connect the two color-1 endpoints by a diagonal line, preserving other cells.
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    pts = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v == 1]
    if len(pts) >= 2:
        (r1, c1), (r2, c2) = pts[:2]
        dr = 1 if r2 > r1 else -1 if r2 < r1 else 0
        dc = 1 if c2 > c1 else -1 if c2 < c1 else 0
        r, c = r1, c1
        while (r, c) != (r2, c2):
            out[r][c] = 1
            r += dr
            c += dc
        out[r2][c2] = 1
    return out

def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    ones = [(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 1]
    sixes = [(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 6]
    # A pair of 1s on a diagonal defines a connecting diagonal segment.
    slope = None
    for i, (r1,c1) in enumerate(ones):
        for r2,c2 in ones[i+1:]:
            if abs(r2-r1) == abs(c2-c1) and r2 != r1:
                slope = 1 if (r2-r1)*(c2-c1) > 0 else -1
                dr = 1 if r2 > r1 else -1
                dc = 1 if c2 > c1 else -1
                r,c = r1,c1
                while True:
                    if out[r][c] != 6:
                        out[r][c] = 1
                    if (r,c) == (r2,c2):
                        break
                    r += dr; c += dc
    # A 6 situated on that diagonal marks the crossing; extend its perpendicular 6-line.
    if slope is not None:
        for r,c in sixes:
            if any((r-r1)*(c-c1) >= 0 and abs(r-r1)==abs(c-c1) for r1,c1 in ones):
                # If 1-line has slope +1, the crossing 6-line has slope -1, and vice versa.
                dr, dc = 1, -slope
                rr,cc=r,c
                while 0 <= rr < h and 0 <= cc < w:
                    if out[rr][cc] != 1:
                        out[rr][cc]=6
                    rr += dr; cc += dc
                rr,cc=r-dr,c-dc
                while 0 <= rr < h and 0 <= cc < w:
                    if out[rr][cc] != 1:
                        out[rr][cc]=6
                    rr -= dr; cc -= dc
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    ones = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 1]
    sixes = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 6]
    # Find the diagonal segment joining the two 1 markers.
    pair = None
    for i, p in enumerate(ones):
        for q in ones[i + 1:]:
            if abs(q[0] - p[0]) == abs(q[1] - p[1]) and q[0] != p[0]:
                pair = (p, q)
                break
        if pair:
            break
    if pair:
        (r1, c1), (r2, c2) = pair
        dr = 1 if r2 > r1 else -1
        dc = 1 if c2 > c1 else -1
        r, c = r1, c1
        segment = set()
        while True:
            segment.add((r, c))
            if (r, c) != (r1, c1) and grid[r][c] != 6:
                out[r][c] = 1
            if (r, c) == (r2, c2):
                break
            r += dr
            c += dc
        # A 6 where the 1 diagonal crosses is extended across the grid on
        # the other diagonal, without overwriting the 1 segment.
        for r, c in sixes:
            if (r, c) in segment:
                for rr in range(h):
                    cc = c - (rr - r) * dc * dr
                    if 0 <= cc < w and out[rr][cc] != 1:
                        out[rr][cc] = 6
    return out
PY
